Question: How can I convert copyrighted YouTube videos to copyright-free YouTube videos?
Old_Answer: If you wait until 70 years after the death of the videos’ creator, you should be OK.
Answer_with_writing_sample: You can't convert copyrighted YouTube videos into copyright-free videos. That’s just not how copyright works. If a video is copyrighted, that means it’s owned by someone, and you can't just magically strip away those rights. You might think you can use editing tools, but that's a slippery slope into copyright infringement territory, and trust me, you don’t want to go there. You’re opening yourself up to potential legal trouble by using someone else's content without permission. Sure, you can find royalty-free materials or create your own original content, but you can't take a copyrighted video and just change it around to make it yours. The only way to use someone else's video legally is to get their explicit permission or to use content that’s licensed under Creative Commons, which lets you know exactly what you can and can’t do with it. YouTube also has its own set of guidelines when it comes to copyright, so make sure to familiarize yourself with those. In short, if you’re thinking you can just repackage someone else's hard work for your own gain, you're mistaken. Respect intellectual property rights. Create your own stuff or use content that’s free and clear, and you’ll save yourself a lot of headaches down the line.
